newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-UNHAPPY RETURN FOR FORMER CHAMPION GERASCH.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-UNHAPPY RETURN FOR FORMER CHAMPION GERASCH.

text.p: Former world champion Sylvia Gerasch completed a miserable international championship return after a two-year suspension when she failed to qualify for her second final at the European sprints and short-course championships on Sunday.

Gerasch, 100 metres breaststroke world champion for East Germany back in 1986, was banned for two years after a positive drugs test at the European sprint championships in November 1993 in Gateshead, England, where she won the 50 breaststroke.
She was found to have excessive levels of the stimulant caffeine in her body. She blamed the positive test on coffee and tried in vain to persuade international swimming leaders to reduce the ban.
Gerasch competed at a World Cup meeting in Imperia, Italy, last February but the Rostock meeting was her first full international championships since the ban.
Gerasch, European 100 breaststroke champion in 1985 and 1993, failed to make the German Olympic team this year and had no luck at these championships.

Now 27, she competed here in the 50 and 100 breaststroke but missed the final in each by one place. She finished seventh overall both times -- 0.32 seconds behind the slowest qualifier in Friday's 100 and 0.11 outside in Sunday's 50.

In contrast, big Dutchman Marcel Wouda looked set to complete an individual medley treble in the Neptun pool after leading qualifiers in heats for the final at 400 metres, having already won the 100 and 200 events.
Wouda, Atlanta Olympic finalist in the 200 and 400 individual medley, swam well within himself but still clocked the fastest heat time of four minutes 16.96 seconds.
Germans Uwe Volk (4:17.54) and Christian Keller (4:21.77) were the next-fastest qualifiers.
Sandra Voelker, who has broken two European records in these four-day championships, sounded her challenge for a third individual title with the fastest heat time in the women's 50 metres backstroke.
Voelker won her heat in 28.49, quicker than the 28.81 clocked by fellow German Antje Buschschulte in the preceding heat.
Sweden's Johanna Sjoberg, who beat Voelker into second place and set European records in the 50 and 100 butterfly finals, managed only the third-fastest time in the 200 butterfly heats.
Sjoberg returned a time of 2:14.72. Barbara Franco of Spain (2:12.62) and Katrin Jaeke of Germany (2:14.24) were faster.
